hints.text: Multiplying by one hundred makes a number much bigger. Think about how far each digit moves and in which direction.
$100$ has two zeros, so the digits of $3.6$ shift two places to the left. One shift makes $36$, and the second shift needs a zero in the ones place.
The second shift turns $36$ into $360$, so $3.6 \times 100 = 360$.

explanation: Since $100 = 10 \times 10$, multiplying by it shifts the digits two places, the same as moving the decimal point two places right.
Start at $3.6$. One shift gives $36$, and the second shift gives $360$, with a zero filling the empty ones place.
So $3.6 \times 100 = 360$, which is reasonable because it is a little more than $3 \times 100$.
